key_insight: Quantum classifiers can achieve competitive overall performance while retaining subgroup disparities, and smaller fairness gaps can mask degraded discrimination.
clinical_relevance: Medical imaging AI should be evaluated for both subgroup disparities and preserved overall performance before clinical use.
method: Audited SVM, MLP, QSVM and QCNN classifiers using ResNet-18 image embeddings.
Compared baseline training with Equalized Odds regularisation, Gradient Reversal Learning and their combination.
Assessed subgroup AUC gaps and non-inferiority to baseline, with PanDerm and EVA-X as external references.
evidence_signal: Across DDI skin-type groups and CheXpert-derived age groups, mitigation effects varied: QSVM with combined mitigation had the best DDI trade-off, while QCNN with Gradient Reversal Learning led aggregate performance on CheXpert but increased disparity.
watch_item: All quantum models ran in classical simulation; the study claims no quantum advantage.
paper_title: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Sensitive Subgroups
